claims.text: Large language models are prone to hallucination, generating plausible yet nonfactual content.
LLM hallucinations can be categorized into two primary types: factuality hallucination and faithfulness hallucination.
Factuality hallucination comprises factual contradiction and factual fabrication.
Faithfulness hallucination comprises instruction inconsistency, context inconsistency, and logical inconsistency.
Contributors to LLM hallucinations span data, training, and inference stages.
Elevating the sampling temperature in stochastic sampling decoding strategies increases the risk of hallucinations.
Incorporating new factual knowledge during supervised fine-tuning correlates with increased hallucinations.

methodologies.name: Literature Survey and Taxonomy Framework Formulation
methodologies.description: A systematic survey methodology that categorizes LLM hallucination phenomena, causes, detection techniques, and mitigation approaches across data, training, and inference dimensions.

limitations.text: Locate-then-edit model editing techniques lack non-trivial generalization capabilities across architectures and empirically only perform well on decoder-only LLMs.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems remain susceptible to retrieval failure and generation bottlenecks, such as the lost-in-the-middle context utilization curse.
